content.title: About
content.content: Pecans are the edible seeds of the pecan tree (Carya illinoinensis), native to North America. The nuts have a sweet, buttery flavor and a crunchy texture. Pecans are eaten raw, roasted, and are used in baking, desserts, sauces, and as pecan oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pecans belong to the hickory family and are closely related to the American walnut.
The seed lies inside a hard shell that is covered by a thin skin.
Pecan trees thrive in warm climates, especially in the United States (Georgia, Texas, New Mexico) and some Asian regions.
Pecans are used to produce pecan oil, flour, and caramelized nut mixes.
The harvest season typically begins in late autumn.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Pecans contain a high amount of monounsaturated fats, which support heart health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: They provide vitamin E and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains magnesium and zinc
items.content: These minerals aid muscle function, nervous system activity, and immune response.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Pecans help maintain satiety thanks to a combination of plant protein and dietary fiber.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: The nuts contain calcium and phosphorus, important for bone tissue.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pecans, ranging up to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Pecans are calorie-dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole pecans can pose a choking risk for young children.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Pecans contain oxalates, which should be limited by people prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pecans can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, and desserts. They are often used in caramelized mixes, as pecan oil, or ground into flour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pecans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts with a rancid or off smell.
